sentences.text: Oligocolius is an extinct genus of mousebird from the Oligocene epoch of Germany that belongs to the family Coliidae.

Unlike modern mousebirds, the skull and beak of Oligocolius closely resemble those of parrots, featuring a broad intertemporal region and a deep, rounded upper beak that was possibly hooked at the tip.
The upper beak was freely mobile due to a hinge between the nasal bones and frontals, while the mandible possessed a particularly long retroarticular process where jaw-opening muscles attach.
The tarsometatarsus of Oligocolius was much shorter than its humerus and ulna, a trait unlike any other known coliiform.
Fossil evidence shows O. psittacocephalon contained many fruit stones inside its body, mostly clustered beneath the skull, and these stones were about 0.5 mm in size and completely intact.
Longer, stronger wings allowed Oligocolius to fly longer distances than living mousebirds.

The genus Oligocolius was described by the authority Mayr in the year 2000 after the first specimen was found in a clay pit at Frauenweiler near Wiesloch, Germany, dating to approximately 32 million years ago.
A second specimen was described by Mayr in 2013 from the 24.7 million-year-old Enspel lagerstätte.
Evidence indicates Oligocolius consumed larger fruits than living mousebirds and swallowed them whole, and the presence of a crop implies it fed on tougher fruits and vegetation.
Researchers infer that the crop evolved independently in Oligocolius since it is absent in living mousebirds and their close relatives.
Oligocolius likely spent more time in trees and dispersed more easily than other coliids.
Oligocolius is the only known coliid from the Oligocene epoch, and the parent group of Oligocolius is the family Coliidae.
Oligocolius lived during the Early to Late Oligocene epoch, with a time range from the Rupelian to the Chattian stages, between 33.9 and 23.04 million years ago.
It is uncertain if Oligocolius's adaptations were a response to a cooling climate in Europe between the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum and the Miocene Climatic Optimum.
